reason: Alert 1 (java/xss): alert-TP — resolved sink value includes user input: The value of 'sql' (which contains user input via 'bar') is passed to encodeForHTML() and then concatenated into the HTML response at lines 61-62. Although HTML encoding is applied, the XSS vulnerability exists because the encoded SQL string is still part of the HTML output, and the original user input flows into the sink expression. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): alert-TP — resolved sink value bar = param because the switch condition 'B' is always met (guess.charAt(1) is 'B'), so param flows directly into the SQL query string at line 56. Case TP: at least one alert-TP.
